about.credits_text: Made by cleitinhodev / bugzinho. Built with Rust, egui and wgpu. Includes Noto Sans CJK (SIL Open Font License 1.1). Thanks to everyone who contributes!
about.description: A painting program made for 360° panoramas — paint directly on the sphere, with layers, brushes and VR-ready export.
about.license: Free software under the MIT license.
about.title: About
brush.flow_tip: Paint laid by each dab (density). Lower values build up.
brush.polar_tip: Keeps the brush round on the sphere by stretching dabs near the poles of the flat image.
brush.pressure_feel_tip: Negative: needs more pressure. Positive: reaches full size and density with a light touch.
brush.smoothing_tip: Stabilizer: smooths the stroke and removes hand shake.

export.desc: Flattens all visible layers into a JPEG that 360° viewers (Facebook, Google Photos, VR headsets…) recognise.
export.gpano_tip: Adds the Photo Sphere XMP tags so websites show the image as an interactive panorama.
export.title: Export 360° JPG
eyedropper.hint: Click or drag on the canvas to pick a color. Right-click a swatch to set the secondary color.
fill.hint: Click an area to fill it. The fill continues across the left/right seam.
help.gesture.line: Straight line from the last stroke
help.gesture.line_delete: Delete the selected point or stroke
help.gesture.line_drag: Move a point or the whole stroke
help.gesture.line_split: Split the stroke at a point
help.gesture.pinch: Zoom and rotate on touch screens
help.lines.desc: A line layer keeps editable strokes instead of pixels: move points, change the thickness of each point or of the whole stroke, the color, opacity and tapers at any time. The lines follow the sphere (they cross the 360° seam and the poles) and blend with the other layers like any layer. Use “Convert to normal layer” to paint over them with the brushes.
help.lines.title: Line layers (vector)
help.place.desc: Drop, paste (Ctrl+Shift+V) or insert an image to float it over the panorama. Move, scale, rotate and flip it with the handles, choose Wrap or Persistent projection, press D to distort it with corner pins or a mesh warp, then press Enter to merge.
help.shortcuts_intro: Every shortcut works in both the sphere and the flat view. On macOS, Ctrl is ⌘.
help.styles.desc: Every painting tool has styles (Oil, Dry brush, Watercolour, Spray, Pencil…) and tip shapes with previews. The Brush mixes with the colours on the layer: adjust Blending, Dilution, Persistence and Irregularity. Raise Spray on the Airbrush to scatter particles. Save your own settings with “Save style”.
help.styles.title: Styles, mixing and particles
help.tip.1: Paint in the sphere view: what you draw is projected exactly onto the panorama, so lines stay straight in 360°.
help.tip.10: Placing a photo or logo? Use Persistent to keep it undistorted from one viewpoint, or Wrap to stick it onto the sphere. Hold Shift while dropping a 2:1 image to open it as a new panorama instead.
help.tip.11: Fitting a picture onto a wall? Place it in Persistent mode looking at the wall, press D and drag the four pins onto the wall’s corners — the perspective stays correct, so it looks like part of the scene.
help.tip.12: Oil mixing works on the active layer: paint the base colours and the new strokes on the same layer to blend them. Mixing and textures follow the sphere, so they also work across the 0°/360° seam and near the poles.
help.tip.13: Line layers stay editable: pick Edit points (K) to move or insert points and Thickness (T) to swell or thin a line point by point. Undo works for every change.
help.tip.14: With “Smooth curve” off, the segments are straight great-circle arcs: they look straight in the 360° view. Shift+click places a sharp corner on a smooth curve.
help.tip.2: The flat view shows the whole equirectangular image. Dimmed copies on each side show how the seam wraps around.
help.tip.3: Turn on the grid (G) to see the horizon and lines every 15° — the equator is highlighted.
help.tip.4: Keep the image at a 2:1 ratio (e.g. 4096 × 2048) so 360° viewers display it correctly.
help.tip.5: Export 360° JPG embeds GPano metadata, so Facebook, Google Photos and VR viewers open it as a panorama.
help.tip.6: Use “Rotate heading” to choose which direction the viewer faces when the panorama opens.
help.tip.7: Lock transparency on a layer to shade inside existing strokes without painting outside them.
help.tip.8: Projects (.pano) keep every layer, blend mode and opacity. Your work is backed up automatically.
help.tip.9: Custom brushes: import Photoshop .abr, GIMP .gbr/.gih or any PNG as a brush tip. Brushes are stamped on the sphere, so they look the same at the poles and across the seam.
help.title: Help
hint.show_ui: Press Tab to show the interface
layer.alpha_lock.desc: When locked, painting only affects pixels that already exist on the layer — perfect for shading.
lines.apply_settings_tip: Applies the size, opacity, tapers and color of the new-line settings
lines.auto_layer: Drawing creates a line layer above the active layer.
lines.corner_tip: The line bends sharply at this point
lines.hint.curve: Click to add points, Shift+click for corners. Double-click or Enter finishes, Esc cancels, Backspace removes the last point.
lines.hint.edit: Drag points or lines. Ctrl+click: insert point / corner. Alt+click: split. Del: delete.
lines.hint.free: Draw freely; the line becomes editable points when you release.
lines.hint.width: Drag a point or a line to change its thickness. Ctrl+click applies the current settings.
lines.no_layer: Select a line layer or create one.
lines.rasterize_tip: Turns the lines into pixels so you can paint over them (undoable)
lines.select_hint: Click a line to select it.
lines.smooth_tip: On: the line curves through the points. Off: straight segments (great circles).
lines.snap_join_tip: Dropping an end point on another end point joins the lines
lines.split_tip: Splits the line in two at this point
mix.blending_tip: How much of the colour under the brush mixes into the paint.
mix.dilution_tip: Thins the paint out over transparent areas, like watery paint.
mix.hint: Picks up the colours on the active layer while you paint.
mix.irregularity_tip: Broken, uneven mixing and dry gaps along the bristles, like a real canvas.
mix.persistence_tip: How long the picked-up colour stays in the brush — high values drag colours along the stroke.
mix.pigment_tip: Subtractive mixing: yellow and blue make green instead of grey.
mix.title: Paint mixing
new.title: New panorama
offset.desc: Shifts every layer horizontally around the sphere, changing where the panorama starts. Nothing is lost.
offset.title: Rotate heading
place.distort.concave: Pins can’t cross or make a concave shape — the last valid shape was kept.
place.distort.degenerate: The shape is too thin — the last valid shape was kept.
place.distort.desc: Drag the corner pins to change the image’s perspective — e.g. to fit it onto a wall or a screen in the scene.
place.distort.hint: Drag the pins onto the corners of the surface (Shift: lock axis) · drag inside to move · D returns to transform
place.distort.perspective.desc: 4 corner pins: a true perspective (homography) — straight lines stay straight. Drag an edge to move both of its pins.
place.distort.warp.desc: A 4×4 mesh on top of the perspective, for curved or uneven surfaces.
place.hint: Drag to move · corners scale (Shift: free) · knob rotates (Shift: 15°) · right-drag looks around
place.merge.desc: Paints the placed image into the active layer at full quality (Enter).
place.mode.persistent.desc: Projects the image like a flat picture seen from the center: looking from the anchored direction it appears undistorted.
place.mode.wrap.desc: Bends the image onto the sphere like a sticker: it keeps its size in degrees wherever you move it.
place.reaim.desc: Moves the projector to the current view direction, so the image faces you undistorted again.
place.title: Place image
place.toast.hint: Adjust the image, then press Enter to merge or Esc to cancel.
place.toast.nothing: The image doesn’t cover any pixel — nothing was merged.
recovery.desc: Panoraminal found an automatic backup from {when}. Do you want to restore it?
recovery.title: Recover unsaved work?
settings.confirm_close: Ask before closing with unsaved changes
settings.embed_brushes_tip: Saves the custom brushes you used inside the .pano file, so the project opens with them on another computer.
settings.pen_pressure_tip: Uses pressure from pens and touch screens when the system reports it.
settings.title: Settings
spray.hint: Raise Spray to scatter the paint as particles.
spray.title: Particles (spray)
style.blender.desc: Mostly smudges and blends the colours already painted.
style.classic.desc: The round brush of Panoraminal 1.0–1.2, without mixing.
style.dry_brush.desc: Little paint on dry bristles: broken strokes that let the canvas show through.
style.grainy.desc: A soft airbrush broken by a fine grain.
style.ink.desc: Sharp, hard-edged lines for line art.
style.marker.desc: A flat, chisel-tipped marker that blends a little.
style.oil.desc: Picks up and mixes the colours under it, with bristle streaks and a broken, uneven mix — like oil paint on canvas.
style.pencil.desc: A grainy pencil that follows the paper texture; pressure controls the density.
style.save_tip: Save the current settings as a style of this tool. Right-click a saved style to delete it.
style.soft.desc: The smooth, low-flow airbrush that builds up colour.
style.soft_eraser.desc: A big, soft eraser that fades gradually.
style.splatter.desc: Big drops flicked around the stroke.
style.spray.desc: A spray can: fine particles around a soft core.
style.textured_eraser.desc: Erases with a chalky, broken edge.
style.title: Styles
style.watercolor.desc: Diluted, transparent paint that thins out over empty areas.
tex.title: Texture
tip.title: Tip shape
toast.downscaled: Image was large and has been resized to {w} × {h}
toast.last_layer: The last layer cannot be deleted
toast.legacy_imported: Imported a Paint360 project — save it as .pano
toast.lines_paint: Painting tools don't work on a line layer — use the line tools or convert it to a normal layer
toast.lines_rasterized: Line layer converted to a normal layer
toast.not_2_1: This image is not 2:1 — it may look stretched on the sphere
toast.not_line_layer: The active layer is not a line layer
tool.airbrush.desc: Very soft, low-flow spray that builds up colour gradually. Raise Spray to scatter it as particles (Spray and Splatter styles).
tool.brush.desc: Oil brush: picks up and mixes the colours on the layer, with bristle streaks and an uneven, canvas-like mix. Choose another style (Watercolour, Blender, Classic…) in the brush card.
tool.custom.desc: Paints with any brush from your library — built-ins, Photoshop ABR, GIMP GBR/GIH or your own images — with spacing, angle, scatter and jitter.
tool.eraser.desc: Erases to transparency on the active layer. Uses its own size and softness.
tool.eyedropper.desc: Click or drag on the panorama to pick the visible color. Hold Alt with any brush for a quick pick.
tool.fill.desc: Fills a connected area with the primary color. The fill wraps around the 360° seam.
tool.line_curve.desc: Click to place points and the line curves smoothly through them (Shift+click: sharp corner). Double-click or Enter finishes, clicking the first point closes the shape. Creates a line layer if needed.
tool.line_edit.desc: Drag points to move them or drag a line to move the whole stroke. Ctrl+click adds a point, Ctrl+click on a point toggles a corner, Alt+click splits, Delete removes. Drop an end point on another to join them.
tool.line_free.desc: Draw freely: when you release, the stroke becomes an editable line with control points. Pen pressure sets the thickness of each point.
tool.line_width.desc: Drag a point to make the line thicker or thinner there, or drag the line to change the whole stroke. Ctrl+click applies the current size, color, opacity and tapers.
tool.pen.desc: Crisp, hard-edged lines. Great for line art and details.
unsaved.desc: “{file}” has changes that have not been saved. Save before continuing?
unsaved.title: Unsaved changes
